scope: Local authentication and unchanged remote policy
Exact Host and Origin validation across OAuth and MCP
Private Unix socket and matching effective UID
Foreground host/client shutdown and replacement lifecycle
Local UI account command routing and absence of automatic remote account dependencies

findings.description: start_local disabled account/guide probes but /login still entered the existing default remote account login task.
findings.resolution: AccountStatus::Local is initialized by start_local; chat_login rejects before starting a task and explains the current MCP URL plus one-use login code. Focused test preserves the draft and verifies no login task or queued action.

conclusions: Local listener accepts only literal loopback binds. Optional NAME.local HTTPS origin requires an explicit fixed loopback port for an existing TLS proxy.
Both ends of the Unix stream compare peer credentials to the effective UID. A random private directory and socket use modes 0700 and 0600; validation rejects symlinks/exposed permissions.
local_router layers exact single Host and exact present Origin checks over all local OAuth and MCP routes; account, enrollment and commerce routes are not mounted.

Only explicit local factories can disable GitHub providers or use the non-Secure loopback cookie. Existing remote identity construction remains HTTPS and existing OAuth constructors keep Secure cookies.
MCP access still uses one-use connection-code OAuth, PKCE/resource checks and a live connection-bound authorization; HTTP loopback access alone is not authorization.
Local parsing does not select or persist a default remote account. Account probes, guide probes and remote logout targets are absent for local mode.
Host cleanup is awaited before watchdog replacement/reexec, signals and closes owned broker connections, aborts bounded owned tasks if needed, and removes only the recorded private socket directory.
The /login routing finding is closed by the final checkpoint. No other blocking source issue found within this focused review.
limits: Source review only; no Cargo, actual login, deployment or workflow dispatch performed by this reviewer.
The final local candidate still requires root's unified compilation and real isolated OAuth/PTY/termination validation.
Pure local mode is currently Linux foreground mode; NAME.local resolution, certificates and TLS proxy are explicitly user-provided rather than automatically configured.
The loopback origin and local same-UID trust boundary do not make notification acceptance evidence of user consent.
